text: Scheme: Mukhyamantri Saur Swarojgar Yojana Ministry: Government of Uttarakhand - Department of Energy & Water Resources Level: state State: Uttarakhand Category: Utility & Sanitation The scheme “Mukhyamantri Saur Swarojgar Yojana” is implemented by the Uttarakhand Renewable Energy Development Agency (UREDA) under the Department of Energy, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote self-employment among the residents of Uttarakhand by enabling them to establish and operate solar power projects, thereby generating clean energy, providing a sustainable source of income, and encouraging entrepreneurship.

title: Mukhyamantri Saur Swarojgar Yojana
ministry: Government of Uttarakhand - Department of Energy & Water Resources
text: Scheme: Mukhyamantri Saur Swarojgar Yojana - Benefits Free 150-200 units domestic electricity or up to 50% state top-up subsidy on domestic solar rooftop plants. Under the scheme, self-employment is provided to eligible applicants/beneficiaries through the allocation of solar power projects with capacities of 20, 25, 50, 100, and 200 kW, as detailed below: - 20 kW: Project cost ₹10 lakh; land required – 300 sq. meters. - 25 kW: Project cost ₹12.50 lakh; land required – 300 sq. meters. - 50 kW: Project cost ₹25.00 lakh; land required – 700–1000 sq. meters. - 100 kW: Project cost ₹50.00 lakh; land required – 1500–2000 sq. meters. - 200 kW: Project cost ₹100.00 lakh; land required – 3000–4000 sq. meters. ***(Selected candidates will be provided loans from Uttarakhand State/District Cooperative Banks at an interest rate of 8%. Additionally, beneficiaries will be eligible for incentives and benefits under the MSME Policy-2023, provided by the Industries Department.)*** The electricity generated from the allotted solar projects will be purchased by Uttarakhand Power Corporation Limited (UPCL) for a period of 25 years. Payments to beneficiaries will be made according to the prevailing tariff rates for the electricity sold.

ministry: Government of West Bengal - Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
text:
Scheme: Krishak Bandhu Scheme
Ministry: Government of West Bengal - Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Level: state
State: West Bengal
Category: Agriculture, Rural & Environment

Launched in 2019, the scheme &quot;Krishak Bandhu Scheme&quot; by the Department of Agriculture, Government of West Bengal, aims to provide financial assistance to farmers for agricultural sustainability and risk mitigation. The scheme offers ₹5,000/- per acre per year as direct income support and ₹2,00,000/- as death benefit to the family of deceased farmers. Eligible beneficiaries include small and marginal farmers owning up to 2 acres of land and all farmer families in case of death or disability. The scheme is implemented by the Department of Agriculture, Government of West Bengal, and applications are accepted both online and offline.

title: Krishak Bandhu Scheme
ministry: Government of West Bengal - Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
text:
Scheme: Krishak Bandhu Scheme - Benefits
Direct financial support of ₹10,000 per year for procurement of quality seeds, fertilizers, and farm equipment inputs.
**Direct Income Support**

  - Farmers with one acre or more of cultivable land receive ₹10,000/- per annum, payable in two equal installments of ₹5,000/- each (one for Kharif and one for Rabi season).
  - Farmers with less than one acre of cultivable land receive assistance on a pro-rata basis, subject to a minimum of ₹4,000/- per annum, paid in two equal installments.

**Death/Disability Benefit**

  - In the event of the death of a farmer between the ages of 18 and 60 years, a one-time lump sum grant of ₹2,00,000/- is provided to the legal heirs of the deceased. The farmer must have been enrolled under the Krishak Bandhu scheme at the time of death.


  - A one-time lump sum grant of ₹2,00,000/- for permanent disability of the farmer due to accident.

**Disbursement Conditions**

  - Income support is linked to land ownership records.
  - Death benefit requires submission of legal heir certificates.
  - Disbursed via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the beneficiary&amp;#39;s bank account.

title: Krishak Bandhu Scheme
ministry: Government of West Bengal - Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
text:
Scheme: Krishak Bandhu Scheme - Frequently Asked Questions Q: What are the eligibility criteria for receiving direct income support under this agricultural scheme? A: To qualify, you must be a resident of West Bengal, own cultivable land (up to 2 acres), and be actively engaged in farming. Q: How much financial assistance is provided per acre under the income support component? A: Eligible farmers receive ₹5,000/- per acre per year, with a maximum limit of 2 acres. Q: Is there a maximum landholding limit to be eligible for the annual income support? A: Yes, only farmers owning up to 2 acres of cultivable land can avail of the income support. Q: How is the annual income support amount disbursed to eligible farmers? A: The amount is paid in two equal installments, corresponding to the Kharif and Rabi seasons. Q: What benefits are provided in case of a farmer’s death under this scheme? A: The family of the deceased farmer receives a one-time payment of ₹2,00,000/- as financial support. Q: Who is eligible to claim the death benefit under this agricultural scheme? A: The deceased must have been a farmer aged between 18–60 years, and the claimant must be the legal heir. Q: What is the financial assistance provided in case of permanent disability due to an accident? A: Farmers who suffer permanent disability due to accidents receive a one-time payment of ₹2,00,000/-. Q: What age group is eligible for the death and disability benefits under this scheme? A: Only farmers between 18–60 years of age are covered under the death and disability benefits. Q: What documents are required to apply for the direct income support component? A: You need an Aadhaar card (linked to a bank account), land ownership proof, and a bank passbook copy. Q: What proof is needed to verify land ownership for income support eligibility? A: A Record of Rights (RoR) or Pattadar Passbook serves as valid land ownership proof. Q: What documents must be submitted to claim the death benefit for a deceased farmer? A: The applicant must provide a death certificate, legal heir certificate, and the farmer’s Aadhaar and land records. Q: Is a disability certificate required to claim the disability benefit under this scheme? A: Yes, a valid disability certificate must be submitted to claim the ₹2,00,000/- disability benefit. Q: What is the official website where I can apply online for this scheme? A: The application can be submitted at https://krishakbandhu.wb.gov.in/users/sign_up.
Q: Is there a helpline number available for queries related to this scheme? A: Yes, you can call 8336957370 or 6291720406 between 10 AM and 6 PM for assistance. Q: What is the official email address for contacting scheme authorities? A: You can email your queries to krishak.bandhu@ingreens.in for support. Q: Can I track the status of my application after submission? A: Yes, you can check your application status on the official website: https://krishakbandhu.wb.gov.in.

title: Jai Bangla Pension Scheme
ministry: Government of West Bengal - Department of Social Welfare
text:
Scheme: Jai Bangla Pension Scheme - Frequently Asked Questions
Q: Who can register as a beneficiary under the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board of Karnataka?
A: Any construction worker whose age is minimum 18 years of age and has worked in any construction work for a minimum of 90 days in a year, are eligible to register as a beneficiary under the Board.

Q: Is there a minimum service requirement to register as a beneficiary?
A: Yes, the building worker must have completed 90 days of service as a building worker in the preceding 12 months.

Q: Who can apply for the welfare scheme?
A: Any registered worker of the Board can apply for the welfare scheme.

Q: What are the mandatory documents for the registration?
A: The documents required for registration are: Employment Certificate (Form V(A)/V(B)/V(C)/V(D)), Aadhar Card (Self-Attested), Ration Card(non-mandatory), Age Proof (one of them Example: Voter ID Card, Aadhar Card).

Q: How often must a construction worker renew their registration with the Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board?
A: A construction worker must renew their registration every 3 years.

Q: What happens if a worker doesn't renew their registration within the 3-year period?
A: If a worker doesn't renew their registration within the 3-year period, they are granted a 1-year grace period to complete the renewal.

Q: What happens if a worker doesn't renew their registration during the grace period?
A: If the worker fails to renew their registration during the 1-year grace period, their registration will become invalid.

Q: Is there any application fee required for the registration under the Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board?
A: No, as per the guidelines, there is no fee required for the registration.

Q: How to enroll as a beneficiary under the Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board?
A: Applicants can visit the official Website of Karnataka Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (KBOCWWB) to enroll themselves as a beneficiary under the board: https://kbocwwb.karnataka.gov.in/login

Q: What are the eligibility criteria for this pension scheme?
A: To be eligible, a worker must be a registered beneficiary of the BOCW Welfare Board, must have completed 60 years of age, must have been a beneficiary of the Board for at least 3 years prior to reaching 60, and must not be receiving similar benefits from other government schemes.

Q: How much pension can a beneficiary receive under this scheme?
A: A beneficiary can receive a pension of up to [?]3,000 per month under this scheme.

Q: Can a beneficiary receive this pension if they are already getting a pension from another government scheme?
A: No, a beneficiary cannot receive this pension if they are already receiving similar benefits from other government schemes.

Q: What should the legal dependents or heirs do if a pensioner passes away?
A: The legal dependents or heirs must inform the BOCW Welfare Board as soon as possible about the death of the pensioner and submit the death certificate to initiate the process of closing the pensioner's bank account.

Q: Why is it important to inform the Board about the death of a pensioner?
A: Informing the Board about the death of a pensioner is important to ensure that the pension payments are stopped, and the pensioner's bank account is properly closed, preventing any unauthorized transactions.

Q: What documents are required to notify the Board about the death of a pensioner?
A: The legal dependents or heirs need to provide the death certificate of the pensioner to the BOCW Welfare Board.

Q: How to apply for the assistance under this scheme?
A: Applicants should visit the official Website of Karnataka Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (KBOCWWB) to avail the assistance under this scheme: https://kbocwwb.karnataka.gov.in/login

Ministry: Government of West Bengal - Department of Commerce & MSME
Level: state
State: West Bengal
Category: Business & Entrepreneurship

**Taruner Swapno Tab Scheme** is an official flagship initiative administered by the **Government of West Bengal - Department of Commerce & MSME** aimed at uplifting eligible citizens across West Bengal.

The scheme was established under the **Business & Entrepreneurship** portfolio to provide direct financial assistance, socio-economic empowerment, and institutional welfare support to target beneficiaries. Eligible applicants are facilitated with direct benefit transfers (DBT), subsidy components, or protective social security benefits following transparent verification guidelines established by the government.

Under current operating directives, the scheme serves to enhance accessibility for Budding entrepreneurs and artisans seeking to launch new manufacturing or service units. and ensures equitable distribution of government assistance through digital and transparent public service delivery channels.

title: Taruner Swapno Tab Scheme
ministry: Government of West Bengal - Department of Commerce & MSME
text:
Scheme: Taruner Swapno Tab Scheme - Benefits
Up to 35% margin money subsidy on bank loans up to ₹25 lakh for establishing micro-enterprises and service units.
### Key Benefits & Entitlements

* **Core Financial / Welfare Support:** Up to 35% margin money subsidy on bank loans up to ₹25 lakh for establishing micro-enterprises and service units.
* **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT):** Financial assistance and subsidies are deposited directly into the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank account (BSBDA / Jan Dhan compatible).
* **Institutional Safeguards:** Complete waiver of hidden processing charges or intermediary fees; state/central monitoring ensures timely disbursement.
* **Complementary Services:** Eligible beneficiaries may also access associated capacity-building, health cover, or subsidized credit support under allied government programs.

title: Taruner Swapno Tab Scheme
ministry: Government of West Bengal - Department of Commerce & MSME
text:
Scheme: Taruner Swapno Tab Scheme - Eligibility
Budding entrepreneurs and artisans seeking to launch new manufacturing or service units.
### Eligibility Requirements

1. **Residency & Domicile:** The applicant must be a citizen of India and a bona fide permanent resident of **West Bengal** with valid domicile documentation.
2. **Age Bracket:** Age between **18** and **55 years** at the time of application.
3. **Target Beneficiary Profile:** Budding entrepreneurs and artisans seeking to launch new manufacturing or service units.
4. **Gender Eligibility:** Open to **Male, Female, Transgender** applicants.
5. **Income Criterion:** Eligible income categories include: Below ₹1,00,000 per annum, ₹1,00,000 to ₹2,50,000 per annum, ₹2,50,000 to ₹5,00,000 per annum.
6. **Social Categories:** GENERAL, SC, ST, OBC communities.
7. **Applicable Occupations:** Self-employed, Unemployed.
8. **Geographical Coverage:** Beneficiaries residing in Urban and Rural areas.

> **Exclusion Criteria:** Individuals already drawing duplicate central/state pensions under identical heads, or taxpayers filing annual income above designated threshold brackets may be disqualified as per official guidelines.

Gender: male, female, transgender
